reader.requirement: At --std 85 a USE statement generates no executable action: execution starts at the first nondeclarative statement, a declarative section runs only when its condition arises (or by PERFORM per GR3), and the USE sentence itself does nothing.

edition-consulted.switches: ctx.Data.DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 exit filter around the USE procedure call; 85 takes the plain try/finally form (not part of SR2's behaviour)

reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness (report-group qualification at 85) exercises binding, not the never-executed property; no witness for start-up, fall-through or PERFORM of a declarative

probes.printed: START N=0 / NO-FAIL N=0 / S1 RAN N=1 ST1=00 / AFTER PERFORM N=1 / S1 RAN N=2 ST1=23 / AFTER READ N=2 ST1=23
probes.expected: declaratives not entered at start or on success; PERFORM S1 runs only its paragraphs and returns without falling into S2; a failed READ (23, no INVALID KEY) runs S1 and control returns after the READ

probes.printed: the declarative runs only after the failing OPEN and WRITE

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.8.3 SR2  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The USE sentence is consumed by DeclCollectSection into a BoundDeclarative scope and produces no statement in the pc space; the emitted dispatch enters the section's pc range only on the I-O condition or a PERFORM.

refuter.evidence: r2empty2.cob at --std 85: a declarative section whose only content is its USE sentence (S0), PERFORMed from the nondeclarative part, does nothing and returns; PERFORM S1 runs only S1's paragraph; the failed OPEN INPUT of F1 runs S0 (explicit file-name, GR4) and nothing prints: 'START / AFTER PERFORM S0 / S1-P1 / AFTER PERFORM S1 / AFTER OPEN ST1=35' EXIT 0. A first attempt with PERFORM S0 THRU S1 was refused COBOL2186, which is correct at 1985 (§1985 Nucleus PERFORM SR11, both names in the same declarative section), so it is not evidence against the rule. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.8.3 SR2  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'.
